label: Phosphorus, in vivo
reference: PCr at 0 ppm (in vivo convention; PCr lies near -2.5 ppm on the 85% H3PO4 scale, so every in vivo value here is about 2.5 ppm higher than the corresponding H3PO4-referenced number)
note: Downfield is positive and to the left: the PCr to Pi separation is the standard intracellular pH probe and the PCr to beta-ATP separation reports free Mg2+, so both of those gaps move by a few tenths of a ppm between tissues and pathologies.

peaks.name: PE
peaks.note: Phosphomonoester. Needs 1H decoupling or 7T to separate from PC; below 3T the two merge into a single PME hump.

peaks.name: 2,3-DPG a
peaks.note: Blood only, from erythrocytes. Downfield of the 2,3-DPG pair; in vivo both are singlets, shifted from their phantom positions by binding to hemoglobin. Its presence in a cardiac spectrum flags blood contamination of the myocardial signal.

peaks.name: PC
peaks.note: Phosphomonoester. Reported in vivo between 5.9 and 6.3 ppm depending on the study and basis set; centre given here.

peaks.name: 2,3-DPG b
peaks.note: Blood only. The second phosphate of the same molecule; the pair spans roughly 5.4 to 6.9 ppm over the physiological pH and oxygenation range and can swamp myocardial Pi.

peaks.name: Pi
peaks.note: At pH 7.0. Titrates downfield with rising pH between the H2PO4- limit near 3.29 ppm and the HPO4-2 limit near 5.68 ppm, pKa about 6.75: roughly 4.13 ppm at pH 6.5, 5.02 at pH 7.2, 5.23 at pH 7.4. This shift, referenced to PCr, is the Moon-Richards pH measurement.

peaks.name: GPE
peaks.note: Phosphodiester, membrane breakdown product. Nearly pH independent.

peaks.name: GPC
peaks.note: Phosphodiester. Reported 2.76 to 2.95 ppm in vivo; essentially pH independent.

peaks.name: PCr
peaks.note: Singlet, the reference at 0 ppm and effectively pH independent over the physiological range. Dominant in muscle and brain; absent in liver and kidney.

peaks.name: gamma-ATP
peaks.note: Doublet, J(P-P) about 16 to 17 Hz, coupled to beta. Carries a contribution from beta-ADP. Sensitive to pH and free Mg2+.

peaks.name: alpha-ATP
peaks.note: Doublet, J(P-P) about 16 to 17 Hz, coupled to beta. Includes small contributions from alpha-ADP and from NAD(H); the least Mg2+ sensitive of the three.

peaks.name: NADH
peaks.note: Singlet on the upfield foot of alpha-ATP. Separating NADH from NAD+ needs 1H decoupling and 4T or above; total NAD is about 0.3 to 0.5 mM.

peaks.name: UDPG a
peaks.note: Doublet, J(P-P) about 20 Hz. Overlaps NADH and the alpha-ATP foot, so it is usually fitted rather than resolved.

peaks.name: NAD+
peaks.note: Two nearly equivalent phosphates; appears as a narrow multiplet (doublet or quartet under 1H decoupling) centred here. NAD+/NADH gives the cytosolic redox state, about 5.7 in brain.

peaks.name: UDPG b
peaks.note: Doublet, the well-resolved member of the UDPG pair. Prominent in liver (about 2 mM); about 0.2 to 0.3 mM in brain.

peaks.name: beta-ATP
peaks.note: Triplet, J(P-P) about 16 to 17 Hz, coupled to both alpha and gamma. The only resonance arising from pure ATP, and the standard concentration reference. Its separation from PCr is the most Mg2+ sensitive shift in the spectrum; reported near -16.0 to -16.3 ppm.
